title: Tensoring K-injectives with bounded split-projective complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $I^\bullet$ a K-injective cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules: $P^r=0$ outside some finite interval of integers. Assume that for every $r$ there are an integer $N_r\geq0$ and maps $i_r:P^r\to R^{N_r}$ and $p_r:R^{N_r}\to P^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Then $\operatorname{Tot}(I^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)$, with terms $\bigoplus_{a+r=n}I^a\otimes_R P^r$ and differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_P$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], is K-injective. No boundedness of $I^\bullet$ or vanishing of $d_P$ is assumed.

proof.text: Define $D^\bullet=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P^\bullet,R[0])$ by [def-pur-hom-complex]. Thus $D^q=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-q},R)$ and $d_D^q(\phi)=(-1)^{q+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-q-1}$. If $P$ is supported in $[u,v]$, then $D$ is supported in $[-v,-u]$. Precomposition with $p_{-q}$ and $i_{-q}$ gives $D^q\to\mathcal Hom_R(R^{N_{-q}},R)\to D^q$ with composite the identity. Coordinate evaluation identifies the middle module with $R^{N_{-q}}$, so every $D^q$ is a retract of a finite free module.

proof.text: For any module sheaf $E$ that is a retract of $R^N$, tensoring a short exact sequence with $E$ gives a retract of its $N$-fold direct sum. The latter is exact, and kernels and images in a split direct sum are computed summandwise, so the retract is exact. Hence $E$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Apply this to every $D^q$ using Step 1.
The complex $D$ is bounded above by Step 1 and has flat terms by Step 2. Therefore [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] implies that $D$ is K-flat.

For $E=P^r$, write $c_j=p_r(e_j)$ and let $\lambda_j:E\to R$ be the $j$th coordinate of $i_r$, so $\sum_j\lambda_j(y)c_j=y$ and $\sum_j\phi(c_j)\lambda_j=\phi$ for $\phi\in E^\vee$. For any module sheaf $B$, evaluation $B\otimes_R E\to\mathcal Hom_R(E^\vee,B)$ sends $x\otimes y$ to $(\phi\mapsto x\phi(y))$; its inverse sends $f$ to $\sum_j f(\lambda_j)\otimes c_j$, and the two displayed identities give both inverse equations. These formulas commute with restriction on the site, and the bilinear formula induces a sheaf-tensor map by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; internal Hom is [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Since $P$ has finite support, the sums in total degree and the products in Hom degree have only finitely many nonzero factors. Thus these evaluation isomorphisms, multiplied on the summand $I^a\otimes P^r$ by $(-1)^r$, give degreewise isomorphisms $\alpha^n:\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_R P)^n\to\mathcal Hom^n(D,I)$, with nonzero component at $q=-r$, sending $x\otimes y$ to $(\phi\mapsto(-1)^r x\phi(y))$.

proof.text: Let $x$ have degree $a$, $y$ degree $r$, and $n=a+r$. Using the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex], the $q=-r$ component of $d_{\rm Hom}\alpha(x\otimes y)$ sends $\phi$ to $(-1)^r d_Ix\,\phi(y)$. Its $q=-r-1$ component sends $\phi$ to $-(-1)^n(-1)^r(-1)^r x\phi(d_Py)=(-1)^{a+r+1}x\phi(d_Py)$; all other components vanish. These are exactly the images under $\alpha$ of $d_Ix\otimes y$ and $(-1)^a x\otimes d_Py$ in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Consequently $d_{\rm Hom}\alpha=\alpha d_{\rm Tot}$, and the degreewise inverses in Step 4 also commute with differentials by multiplying this equality by the inverses. Thus $\alpha$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text: By Step 3, $D$ is K-flat, and $I$ is K-injective by hypothesis; [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] therefore makes $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,I)$ K-injective. For any map $f:A\to\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_R P)$ from an acyclic complex, $\alpha f$ has a null homotopy $h$ by [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Composing each $h^k$ with $(\alpha^{k-1})^{-1}$ gives a null homotopy of $f$, since $\alpha^{-1}$ is a chain map. This proves K-injectivity of the total complex without a boundedness assumption on $I$.
